title: Ariana Grande’s Eternal Sunshine Tour Surpasses $100 Million in Grosses
summary: The trek broke nine digits from just 41 arena shows.
contentText:
Ariana Grande played the last of 41 shows on The Eternal Sunshine Tour at London’s O2 Arena on Tuesday (Sept. 1). According to figures reported to Billboard Boxscore, the trek grossed $107.9 million and sold 638,000 tickets.

Related

The Eternal Sunshine Tour was relatively short and sweet. By number of shows, it was less than half as long as her last three treks: 2019’s Sweetener World Tour, 2017’s Dangerous Woman Tour and 2015’s The Honeymoon Tour. Accordingly, it earned less than the Sweetener run ($146.4 million) and reported fewer tickets sold than the last two outings (1.3 million and 875,000). But night by night, it packed a bigger punch than any of her previous live shows.

On average, Grande brought in $2.6 million and sold 15,600 tickets per show. Those figures represent jumps of 74% and 14%, respectively, over her previous bests on the Sweetener World Tour ($1.5 million; 13,700 tickets).

The Eternal Sunshine Tour made just 11 stops — nine in the United States, one in Canada and one in the United Kingdom. Ranking all of Grande’s single-venue engagements across her career, her 2026 run occupies the entire top 10 by gross, and eight of the top 10 by attendance. Her 10-night stay in London reigns supreme in both categories, with $27.7 million and 179,000 tickets.

The Eternal Sunshine Tour’s 31 shows in North America combined for $80.2 million and 459,000 tickets, marking the highest grossing leg of any Grande tour.

The Eternal Sunshine Tour was Grande’s first live trek in seven years, following the 2020 release of Positions and the 2024 drop of its namesake Eternal Sunshine . Additionally, within its three-month run, she launched Petal on July 31 as she closed out her three-night stay at Montreal’s Bell Centre. All three albums topped the Billboard 200 and spawned No. 1 songs on the Billboard Hot 100 .

Dating back to her first reported show at The Fillmore in Silver Spring, Md. — $59,000 and 2,000 tickets sold on Aug. 13, 2013, where the most expensive ticket was $32 — Grande has grossed $351.4 million from 3.4 million tickets sold over 270 reported shows.
